utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, I know that the chief of secretariat mentioned that General Lukic, the head of the staff was the head of staff, and I think it was David Gajic if I remember correctly, who was in charge of state security. I may have forgotten the person's name actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about the Urosevac SUP, whether at that level there was co-operation with the organisational units of state security?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, that is precisely why the staff was established. That is to say, to promote co-operation between the two services. After the staff was established, the state security in Urosevac also had closer co-operation with our chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to the police department, how did this co-operation evolve specifically, or within some other organisational unit within the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, the state security department in Urosevac for the most part had closer co-operation with the crime police department of the Urosevac SUP. We took certain operative and tactical measures. For example, when premises were supposed to be searched and so on, when they had plans for searching someone's home, then we would be involved, and the crime police department, and the state security people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any co-operation in terms of bringing persons from the territory that your police department covered when carrying out its regular work?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, members of the police, as they carried out their regular work and tasks through patrols, sectoral work, check-points, and so on -- actually, after that if there were persons who were assumed to have something do with the implementation of terrorist actions, such persons were brought in as suspects to the police station and the policemen would compile reports and hand them over to the OKP, that is to say the crime police department and the state security department there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D106.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's 12 in your binder. Witness, this is a decision of the minister of the interior dated the 19th of July, 1998. It was Vlajko Stojiljkovic at the time. Could you please tell us whether you are aware of this decision, and could you please explain to us what this is all about and what action was taken on the basis of this decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: As you have said, this is a decision made by the minister of the interior of the Republic of Serbia, Vlajko Stojiljkovic. He says: "For having distinguished themselves in carrying out the security task of prevention of terrorism in the area of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija in the period since the 20th of July, 1998, I hereby award members of the PJPs, active and reserve force, members of the SAJ and members of the JSO 50 dinars per person per day for every day of engagement in the tasks relating to item 1 of this decision."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, we can read that. However, in the Urosevac SUP, were payments made on the basis of this decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me just one more thing: The JSO unit, who do they belong to, which sector?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: The state security. They were linked to them, organisationally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have document D109.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's number 13 in your binder, sir. Here we have a letter by the staff in Pristina dated the 3rd of August, 1998. Can you tell us who this was addressed to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is again a letter of the staff sent to the all secretariats in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And to whom in the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: To the chief -- to the chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of this letter?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see here in this first paragraph that there was an assessment that terrorist attacks on cities were possible. So did you take any measures based on this letter? Did you take any measures in the territory of your SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: We certainly did. We would always act upon every letter. We would take up certain measures and activities, and I'm sure that we informed the staff of this and most likely we reinforced our coverage of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any attacks did transpire? Were any cities attacked in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, in my territory, or rather, in the outskirts of Kacanik the town, a police patrol there was attacked as a result of which eight policemen were severely injured. Urosevac, Strpci, Strpci is a small town, were not attacked literally, but the village of Gornje Nerodimlje near Urosevac was. That's in Urosevac municipality. It's a mixed village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what about outside of the Urosevac territory, were there any attacks to your knowledge on other cities and towns in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, I just know from what the media reported that in Orahovac and in some other cities there were attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D108, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's your tab 14. Witness, this is a letter by the MUP staff, letter number 10 from the 3rd of August, 1998. Can you tell us to whom it was sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This letter of the staff was sent to the secretariats in Pristina, Pec, Prizren, Djakovica, Gnjilane, Urosevac, and Kosovska Mitrovica, which is to say to all secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija. To the chiefs and commanders of the PJP detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see the contents of this document, but I'm interested especially in paragraph 2. What did the police department of Urosevac SUP do in relation to what is stated there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, most likely intelligence was received indicating that Albanian terrorists had used medical prescriptions and the like in order to safely leave the area where there were combat operations. It says here what procedures should be used if we come across such persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did your policemen act in accordance with this letter?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember specifically whether we had such cases, but we certainly abided by this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D240, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's tab 15 in your binder. We have here a letter of the MUP staff in Pristina dated 9th of August, 1998. So could you please comment on paragraph 3. Did you implement any measures in your territory, and if so, then which police department did?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I have said earlier, we were duty-bound to act upon any letter or memo we received. But as far as I remember, in relation to the paragraph you mentioned is that we took up measures in the area of village Zborce and Crnoljevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. And what particular measures did you take?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: In that area, there were trenches and other fortifications erected and they needed to be filled in, and we thought that terrorist actions would be terminated by the mere fact that OSCE Mission had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We'll see that this letter is from August?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are quite right, but it was already announced that the OSCE Mission would arrive. Therefore, we started filling in those bunkers, trenches, and shelters in order to continue with our regular work so that people could live normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. And who used those trenches and shelters and so on?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, the Albanian terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what did they do from them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, they attacked members of the army and police, they kidnapped persons, they engaged in activities that were hard to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Crnoljevo and that area, why were they important?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Crnoljevo was important for them in order to paralyse the traffic in that direction in order to cut off the road so that factories and institutions would stop working.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, what road is it that leads to Crnoljevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: That's the Pristina-Stimlje road. And then to Dulje, Suva Reka, and Prizren. This is the road which represents the connection with Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D242, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is tab 16 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch of the MUP staff in Pristina dated 16 September 1998. Could you please tell me, Mr. Mitic, whether you received this dispatch and whether you acted in accordance with it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: All right. I managed to read the first paragraph. I remember this dispatch. This dispatch was sent to all SUPs and all chiefs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and to the commanders of PJPs in Pristina, Kosovska Mitrovica, Pec, Djakovica, and Prizren. Yes, I remember this dispatch. We undertook all measures pursuant to it because there had been such cases and events with certain policemen developed a relaxed attitude when it comes to wearing uniform, they had unkempt appearance and so on, and we undertook all of these measures pursuant to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D243, which is tab 17 in your binder, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from the 17th of September, 1998. A dispatch of the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you receive this dispatch at the Urosevac SUP, and did you act pursuant to it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: The chief certainly received this dispatch. I remember it. In paragraph 1 we can see that the quality of work, safety of police officers, tidiness, and the uniformity of the setup need to be improved. So what were we supposed to do in relation to this? It is stated here in the letter and we acted pursuant to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did your policemen man the check-points that are mentioned in this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: I know that we had a traffic check-point in the village of Grlica. Now, whether it was during this period of time, I think it was, 17th of September, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were regular police duties performed at those check-points?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Routine police work was performed at those check-points. Members of the traffic police from the police station were also present at those check-points, and also general policemen, to call them that. So those were joint check-points, everybody did their work, traffic policemen inspected driving licences, car papers and their validity; whereas, the other policemen inspected trunks, vehicles in order to possibly find unlawful items indicating that there had been crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was there any discrimination when it comes to inspections at these check-points?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: No, there certainly wasn't any discrimination because criminals are criminals regardless of their ethnicity. Certainly the inspection was stepped up so that maybe not all of the vehicles, but most of them were inspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I think it's time for a technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic. We will have the break now and resume at 6.00. There will be an adjournment now for half an hour. The Court Officer will assist you during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please see D1202.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is tab 18 in your binder. This is a dispatch by the public security department of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia dated 18 September 1998. And somebody signed it on behalf of General Vlastimir Djordjevic, chief of the public security department, and I would like to know to whom this was sent, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This was sent to all of the secretariats in Serbia, from the first one to the 33rd one. It was also sent to the head of the MUP staff in Pristina, to border police stations, to all them, to their chiefs, to the chief of Internal Affairs, to the chief of crime police administration, to the chief of border police administration for foreigners and administrative affairs, to the fire prevention police administration, and to the operations centre chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this dispatch from the chief of the SUP to whom it was sent concerning your line of work?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you acted in accordance with this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in view of its nature, what kind of a dispatch is this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This dispatch requests that activities of all services be stepped up. In the security sector, they were supposed to conduct beat patrol, operative and other activities, observe and inspect locations and features in the security sector where explosive devices could be planted and activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, does this pertain to the secretariats of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the entire territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see D244, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a dispatch from the MUP staff in Pristina dated 20th of September, 1998. Can you tell me to whom it was sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent by the staff to all SUPs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija to their chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me, please, the issue of surrender of weapons in September of 1998, what was happening in relation to it and what activities did you undertake regarding it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: When it comes to voluntary surrender of weapons, as far as I can remember contact was made with certain individuals from local self-rule organs, contact was made with them to urge citizens to surrender weapons voluntarily. If police knew that there were weapons in certain locations, they would try to use these peaceful means to urge people to surrender these weapons, to get rid of weapons and to go back to normal life.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D245, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 20. Witness, this is a document sent by the MUP in Pristina on the 2nd of October, 1998. Who to, could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This was also sent by the staff of the Ministry of the Interior in Pristina for Kosovo and Metohija to all the police stations -- or rather, all the SUPs, actually, secretariats, in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with this dispatch, and was it carried out in relation to the persons that it pertains to? Could you give us a bit more detail?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes. The content of the dispatch was conveyed to us. We were told that the session of the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia that was held on the 28th of September, 1998, called upon all of those citizens who had been forcefully armed by Albanian terrorists to continue surrendering their weapons and military equipment to the security organs and they would suffer no consequences as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the territory of Urosevac where you were, were there any areas where these weapons were voluntarily surrendered, and these people were pardoned?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the villagers from Damjak and Varus [phoen] they voluntarily surrendered their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have P1230, or rather, 1203.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 22 in your set of documents. Witness, this is a dispatch sent on the 7th of October, 1998. It was sent by the chief of the public security sector Vlastimir Djordjevic. Could you please tell us what the situation was? It's number 21 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell us what was the security situation like at the moment when this dispatch arrived, and what did you do specifically in relation to this dispatch that arrived at the Urosevac SUP? Who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: You see, this dispatch was sent to all the chiefs of SUPs from 1 through 33 throughout Serbia. Then to all border police stations; then to the ministry staff in Pristina, to the head; then the security institute, to the director; the police academy, to the dean; the college of Internal Affairs to the director; and the secondary school of Internal Affairs, to the director. This dispatch has do with the following: There is a fear that there might be a NATO aggression against our country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What measures did you take at the Urosevac SUP in relation to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, we took the measures that we were instructed to take on the basis of this dispatch, that is to say, to update the defence plans, the mobilisation plan in particular, then to ensure that all work lines are functioning on the territorial and line principles, to raise the overall mobility of the service so that all tasks may be accomplished as efficiently as possible from the entire domain of work of the ministry, and so on and so forth. We took appropriate measures in all of these fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This update of the defence plans, especially the mobilisation plan, which organisational unit did that in the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: The police department, or rather, an officer from that department, the late Grade Zivic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D433.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could we please have page 2 of the document immediately actually. This is a dispatch of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia dated the 8th of October, 1998. Again it's from the public security sector. I would be interested in the following: Did you receive this dispatch, did you act in accordance with it, who was it sent to, which secretariats?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: All the secretariats in the Republic of Serbia, 1 through 33. All of them. And the rest as is stated here. Then there is a reference here to the decree on special measures under conditions of the threat of NATO armed attacks on our country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you discuss this decree at a meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, most probably with the chief of the secretariat. That was discussed at a meeting, and we acted upon it accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see that we are already well into October 1998. We saw that there was a threat of NATO bombing and that plans had to be updated. Do you know anything about the October Agreement that was reached, and what you as the secretariat were supposed to do by way of your own tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I remember it very well. The agreement between the then-president of Yugoslavia Slobodan Milosevic and Holbrooke. On the basis of this agreement, we took all the measures envisaged in the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D107.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, I think it is tab 23 in your binder. It is a dispatch of the MUP staff from Pristina. The date is the 20th of October, 1998. So could you please tell me who it was sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This dispatch -- yes, this dispatch was sent to the police administration to the chief for reference, to the administration for joint affairs, to the chief for reference, then all the SUPs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, or rather, the chief and the commander of the PJP, SAJ, and JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the topic dealt with in this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: The engagement of PJP, SAJ, and JSO members is being rewarded. Let me just have a moment, please. Yes, yes, to compile lists for the period from the 18th of September until the 17th of October, 1998, and that payments be made to the members of those units at a rate of 50 dinars per day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was sent to the PJP, SAJ, and JSO commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this JSO unit, which sector did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: JSO is an abbreviation for the unit for special operations, and it belonged to the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And was -- was the PJP of the Urosevac secretariat rewarded in this way on the basis of this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P769, please. Could we have that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It should be tab 24 in your binder. These are conclusions of the MUP staff dated the 26th of October, 1998, in relation to a meeting held on the 25th of October, 1998 at the staff headquarters in Pristina with the chiefs of secretariats, chiefs of police departments and commanders of PJP detachments. Tell me, did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see here that the meeting was chaired by the assistant minister, Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic. Can you tell us a bit about the subject matter dealt with at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, the meeting was chaired by assistant minister Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic. He informed all of us present there about the latest developments concerning the threat of bombing. As well as with the tasks arising from the agreement on the OSCE Verification Mission in Kosmet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, as for the reduction in the number of police, did the assistant minister inform you about that, and was action taken accordingly?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say that we were made aware of this and the number of policemen was reduced, and as far as I can remember, the army also withdrew from some of its positions. They withdrew into barracks, and all other measures were taken in accordance with the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you can also look at your second page. One of these agreements also envisaged observation points, and I see here Dulje, 6 in parentheses. Did you have any observation posts after the agreement was signed, and if so, where and for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, because this was envisaged by the agreement, and we had six of these observation posts. The reason why they were there was to secure the Stimlje-Dulje road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These observation posts, was it their task to check traffic that was there on that road?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: No, no way. It was just important that the road not be threatened by Albanian terrorists who often attack the road, kidnap people, et cetera, so then these post remained and even possession of arms was observed. 7.9 millimetres was the largest calibre that could be used from that moment onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In accordance with this agreement to the best of your knowledge what did the members of the police and the army do?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Both fully complied with the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The army and the police, did they go back to their regular activities after the agreements were signed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, indeed. The police and the army did their regular work except for these observation posts that we referred to. The police remained there to protect the road from possible attacks by terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, in the period after this agreement was signed, to the best of your recollection what did the KLA do?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my recollection, after the OSCE Mission arrived, the Albanian terrorists took advantage of that period of time to consolidate their forces, to regroup, and they even took territories that had been cleansed of terrorists, if I can put it that way, beforehand. From these territories they continued even more fiercely with kidnappings, attacks against the army and police, that is to say, there was an increase in number of provocations, and many soldiers and policemen got killed, even on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, in your jurisdiction was the Kosovo Verification Mission set up, and did you have any contact with them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: In our region, the OSCE had its headquarters in the town of Urosevac and from the very beginning we had frequent contacts with them. The co-operation started out successfully. However, there were problems. The Albanians frequently complained, they invented certain events and phenomena; whereas, Serbs who sometimes wanted to contact them were not taken seriously, so problems were encountered by both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As for the verification of events, what were your relations with KVM like, and what kind of co-operations did you have with them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When it comes to verification of events, what was your co-operation with KVM like, or rather, with the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: As for that co-operation, they had full access everywhere. They could even monitor and visit policemen at the check-points. They would come to us, heads of organisational units, they had contact with us, they would inform us of problems that had been pointed out by Albanians. We solved those problems and initially all of that functioned without any problems, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you going to complete your thought or have you completed it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: I have completed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that there had been attacks on the police and the army after the Verification Mission arrived. Did they go out to verify those events? Did they visit the sites with some sort of, or rather, aiming to make a record of it? How did that transpire?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: We informed the OSCE Mission in our area regularly about all of the problems. However, when on-site investigations were conducted, they did not come there. They would come a day later or if the event happened in the morning, they would come in the afternoon. They would come to inform themselves of what had happened. On many occasions we tried to get the OSCE Mission to resolve the issue of persons who had been kidnapped, and we always received a negative response from them, which irritated even further people, particularly villagers of Gornje Nerodimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now that you've mentioned kidnapped persons, were Albanians kidnapped by KLA?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: In my territory, people of all ethnicities were kidnapped. All ethnicities. They were Albanian, Serbs, Roma, even Turks and Muslims and others who had been kidnapped. Literally all ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know of the reasons for kidnapping Albanians by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: One of the reasons was to spread fear among the population. That was the main reason. The second one, when it comes to Albanians they mostly kidnap persons who co-operated or had some other sort of contacts with police or the army, or people who socialised with Serbs. This is why some Albanians were kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Prizren SUP, and I'm referring to all organisational units now, were there any members of Albanian ethnic community who worked there in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, in my secretariat there were Albanians who worked both for the public and for the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you give us names of some persons who were active in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll try to remember all of them, but I'm sure that I'll miss someone. I know that Hebib Koka worked in Kacanik. He was an inspector of property crime. Then there was Aziv Haliti from Urosevac also dealing with property crime. Avdi Musa also an inspector for property crime from Urosevac. Bekim Komorani [phoen]. I think he was a traffic policeman. Then the Qerimi brothers. I think they were from Godance village. I don't know if it was Gornje Godance or Donje Godance, but one of them worked in Stimlje, and the other brother worked in Liplje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, among the members of reserve forces, were there any Albanians?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were some in reserve forces as well. One was killed. I think his name was Olluri, Nazmi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you invite representatives of the KVM when you went out on routine police business such as patrols, touring certain places and other activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Most often I contacted a gentleman called Jeff. I think he was from the Netherlands. I had the closest co-operation with him. We would visit certain Albanian families and whatever he insisted on, I tried to help him out with it so that he would gain a realistic picture of what was happening in the territory of our secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that Jeff came to your secretariat in Urosevac. Now, what about in areas where you had OUPs and police stations, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, there as well. Commanders of police stations contacted representatives of OSCE without any problems. They would come regularly to police stations and inquire about certain events. I think I need to point out that those were mostly cases where certain Albanians had been apprehended at check-points and brought in for an interview to the police station, then the OSCE would react, they wanted to inquire about those who had been apprehended and brought in and we would give them information that was relevant, that they were interviewed and released or that they were interviewed and kept in custody if there was evidence to support it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D246.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 25. This is a dispatch by the MUP staff or a memo, I'm not sure. No, it's a dispatch, dated 11 November 1998. Tell us, please, who was it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch, and it was sent by the staff to all secretariats of the interior in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of this dispatch, and if so, how, and what did you do pursuant to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, from what I could read just now, yes, I was aware of this dispatch. The chief of the secretariat made me aware of it. And it says here that permanent duty service of the officer complement should be established and that one platoon for an OUP or police station should be established. So certain measures were envisioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Was this duty service of the officer complement established?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes. We certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And how did you organise this duty service?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I can't tell you how we organised this duty service until what hour in the day. I think maybe I should read this dispatch, but I know for a fact that we had people on duty at least until 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P1204.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is tab 26 for you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Should I comment this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, let's wait until we have it on the screen. This is a dispatch of the public security department, signed by chief of the department, General Vlastimir Djordjevic. Tell me, please, to which SUPs was this dispatch sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: It was sent to all SUPs in the Republic of Serbia from 1 to 33, to their chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the topic of this dispatch, and when it comes to state holidays, what was the procedure?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Well, I retired four months ago, but I can tell you that such dispatches arrived always, even during that period of time. This was written on 25th of November, and always on the eve of the holidays certain measures, security measures were stepped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D003-1200.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 27. Witness, please look at the screen. You see the Serbian version. Can you tell us, please, what is this document, who wrote it, and how, and what is it about? So this document is from 1998. We can't really see the date. It was signed by you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, I signed it. And I wrote this report following my contact with the OSCE Mission. I wrote there what was it that interested the OSCE Mission and what we did in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were such reports written by other individuals in your branch offices outside of Urosevac in relation to their contacts with KVM representatives?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Every contact, if OSCE representatives inquired or requested anything, then the person who was in contact with them was duty-bound to write such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When the reports came from outside of the city of Urosevac, whom were they sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: If these reports were written by police members, rather by commanders and their associates, then it was sent to me. And then I would convey this to the chief of the secretariat via the unit for analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the year of this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This report was written in 1998 at the time when the Kosovo Verification Mission was set up. This is one of the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, I think we need to learn from the witness, and the reason for my asking is that in the heading those typing the translation have put 26 of 1998, whereas in the body of the report, the date is illegible but the year is 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, this is a huge omission on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you please explain this document to us. What is this about? What year --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just the date, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, from this document I really can't see the date. However, it was registered under number 26, that's certain. So the number of this document is 26. At this moment I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, there's a different problem here. What the presiding judge spoke about, do you see here where it says date -- first it says "report" and then it says "date" and then it says "hours." Can you read to us, please, the year?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: I think it says 10 and then another date and then 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. And in the heading what does it say there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: It says that the number of this report is 26 and then it gives the date, and the date is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about the year?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: I think that it was corrected to 1998, but it pertains to 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What do you mean it was corrected to 1998, but it pertains to 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: In the heading where it says "date" I think that the third figure 9 has been corrected. It's either a 8 or a 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly. What is the first figure?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: It says 26/1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. What about the line underneath, it says something there, can you read it for us, I can't?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: It says "date" and then I can't see what date this is, and then it says 199, and I think that the last figure has been changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what figure is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Most likely 1998, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you think that the last figure is 8. All right. And in translation it's also 8. Now, in the body of the text, it says "date" and then it says "1999?"

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes. And there are also some 4s, but I can't really read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. And in the left corner is the registry stamp right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was registered under number 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: I think 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And it was signed by?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: By me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And who did you contact?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: All right. The team comprised, Lesi Piper Tagle, head of the group; Mehmed Akalin; Diego Tramontana; and Ali Maralusi [phoen], interpreter from Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you start having contacts with the members of the Kosovo Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember immediately upon their arrival we established contact and started communicating regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And when did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: I can't really remember exactly, but I think it was in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So starting from October until what time were they there, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: I think until the very beginning of the NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know whether a document of this kind and with these explanations can be admitted into evidence. If not, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received as an exhibit. The date of it or the year of it being unknown, probably either 1998 or 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will be Exhibit D00826.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now please have Exhibit D436.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It should be tab 28 in your binder. This is a dispatch of the chief of public security, General Vlastimir Djordjevic, dated the 11th of December, 1998. First of all, which SUPs was it sent to, this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to all the SUPs, from 1 through 33 of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of this dispatch at the time when it was sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Although, as regards the buying and selling of foreign currency, action Valuta, it was the crime police department that was charge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And tell me covering market squares, et cetera, did members of your department do any work in that respect, and did they react to these things that were supposed to be curbed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were joint actions organised to deal with these problems, so it was the police department and the crime police department that did this, so it was policemen working with inspectors in civilian clothes that handled this, to put it simply.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us more about paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: It is stated here that immediately on the 11th of December, 1998, from 7.00 onwards action should be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have P717.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's tab 29 in your binder. This is a dispatch of the head of the public security department dated the 21st of December, 1998, General Vlastimir Djordjevic. Tell me, which SUPs was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: This dispatch was also sent to all the SUPs, 1 through 33 throughout Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of this dispatch, and did you act accordingly, according to the instructions contained in this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to move on to a completely different topic that will take awhile and our time is almost up for the day. It's just a few minutes that are left, so perhaps we could call it a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the evening, Mr. Djurdjic. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. A Court Officer will assist you when we leave the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
